text:
maya.k: FYI customer ACME reported sudden NXDOMAIN for internal API in prod after we completed AZ peering change this morning.
customer-ops: seeing 503s -> DNS NXDOMAIN when calling api.internal.acme.com from their VPCs.
maya.k: Is this split-horizon/private zone? ask customer if they own a private hosted zone for api.internal.acme.com
customer-ops: yes they use a Route53 Private Hosted Zone attached to a set of VPCs. They also wired Transit Gateway to new AZ VPCs.
devin.s: likely resolver rule assoc issue — TGW peering doesn't auto-associate Resolver rules. Check inbound/outbound endpoints and VPC associations.
maya.k: asked them to run dig +short @172.31.0.2 api.internal.acme.com from one of the affected app instances, waiting on output.
customer-ops: dig returns nothing (no answer) and dig +trace shows no authoritative record.
sophie: can you confirm Route53 hosted zone still exists and hasn't been accidentally deleted? Also check if the hosted zone is associated with the expected VPC IDs.
customer-ops: hosted zone exists and shows two associated VPCs (old ones) — new AZ VPCs missing.
anil: found root cause in similar cases — when TGW attachments are created, Resolver rule associations scoped to account/region may need manual association to the new VPCs or you need outbound endpoints in the peered VPC.
maya.k: asked customer to attach the hosted zone to missing VPCs or create inbound resolver endpoints in the TGW-VPC and ensure route 53 resolver rules point at them.
customer-ops: they tried associating and got RouteAlreadyAssociated error for one VPC ID (weird), they used consolidated accounts.
devin.s: that error often means there's an overlapping private hosted zone with same name in another account — check for duplicate hosted zones (cross-account). Also ensure no resolver-rule priority conflict.
maya.k: requested AWS account/zone IDs and logs; meanwhile disable the failing route in app as temporary workaround and set fallback to public DNS (if acceptable).
sre-bot: alert created INC-2026 linked to this thread.
customer-ops: provided zone id: Z3XXXXX and another hosted zone with same name found in infra-account; looks like DNS shadowing. Removing duplicate assoc fixed it and NXDOMAIN cleared.
maya.k: closing loop — customer re-tested and API OK. Root cause: cross-account duplicate private hosted zone shadowing after TGW attach; manual cleanup needed. Recommend doc update and add a resolver rule checklist for TGW workflows. :thumbsup:
